mainTopic: When a שליח must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם: hearing the writing is enough, the status of בבל, and local rulings based on קיום.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב אשי's ruling: a שליח can say בפני נכתב even if he only heard the scratch of the quill on the parchment. A ברייתא about a שליח and a סופר on different floors supports him. The גמרא then explains the ברייתא's line about going in and out all day: it means a סופר who went to the market and came back, and we do not worry that someone there hired him to write a different גט. Next, רב and שמואל argue whether בבל counts like ארץ ישראל for גיטין. Both agree the concern is קיום, and they argue only over whether the ישיבות make witnesses easy to find. רבי ירמיה challenges רב from the borders in the משנה, then answers himself that בבל is an exception. The גמרא discusses where בבל ends, explains רב חסדא's one-way rule between אקטיספון and בי ארדשיר by who recognizes whose signatures, and shows why רבא required the declaration even within one neighborhood in מחוזא. The amud ends with רב telling רב כהנא that he did not need to make the declaration, and רב's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even hearing the sounds of writing is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי finishes his ruling: the שליח may testify about the writing of the גט even if all he did was hear the quill and the parchment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if he only heard the sound of the pen and the sound of the parchment, that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends רב אשי's statement, which began on the previous amud. He says the שליח does not need to see the writing; hearing it is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שליח has to be able to say the גט was written in his presence, so that we know it was written לשמה, for this specific woman. רב אשי makes the requirement very light: the sound of the writing is enough to count as 'in his presence.'

keyTerms.meaning: The scroll or parchment being written on

phrases.english: Even the sound of the quill
and the sound of the scroll.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's statement, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing the sounds of the writing is enough for the שליח to say בפני נכתב.

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the גט is valid even if the שליח and the סופר were on different floors, and even if someone was going in and out all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רב אשי: when someone brings a גט from overseas, it is valid even if he was in the house and the scribe was in the upper room, or he was upstairs and the scribe was in the house, and even if he was going in and out all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that it says supports רב אשי. The next step will explain how the ברייתא proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows cases where the שליח is on a different floor from the סופר. That suggests the שליח does not need to watch the writing directly. The last clause about going in and out will be questioned later.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view
One who brings a גט from overseas

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with Rav Ashi:
One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas,
even if he was in the house and the scribe was in the loft,
phrases.notes: "He" is the שליח who will later testify about the גט.

phrases.english: or he was in the loft and the scribe was in the house,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא כָּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: even if he was going in and out the whole day, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב אשי's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's ruling that hearing the writing is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a שליח and a סופר on different floors

steps.title: Why the ברייתא proves that hearing is enough
steps.stepSummary: If the שליח is downstairs and the סופר is upstairs, he cannot see the writing. So the ברייתא must mean he heard it, just as רב אשי said.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is in the house and the scribe is in the loft? Then he can't see him! So it must be a case where he heard the sound of the pen and the parchment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא supports רב אשי. It shows that the case in the ברייתא only works if hearing is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When they are on different floors, the שליח cannot see the סופר. Since the ברייתא still calls the גט valid, the שליח's connection to the writing must have come through sound. That is exactly רב אשי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not rather... (introduces the only reasonable reading)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about different floors supports רב אשי: a שליח who only heard the writing can still say בפני נכתב.

phrases.english: He is in the house and the scribe is in the loft?!
But he doesn't see him!
Rather, is it not a case where he heard
the sound of the quill and the sound of the scroll?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו כְּגוֹן דִּשְׁמַע קַן קוּלְמוֹסָא וְקַן מְגִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא proves רב אשי's ruling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's case of the שליח and סופר on different floors, where seeing is impossible

steps.title: Who is the one going in and out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's last clause and asks who it is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: even if he was going in and out the whole day, it is valid. Who is meant?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the ברייתא again and asks who 'he' is. This sets up the next two steps, which try out each possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clause could mean either the שליח or the סופר. Each option will be tested to see whether the clause adds anything new.

phrases.english: The master said:
phrases.notes: This just means "the ברייתא we quoted said." It is going back to look at one line.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא כָּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: Even if he was going in and out the whole day, it is valid.
Who?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the proof to a question about the ברייתא's final clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the one going in and out is the שליח or the סופר.

steps.title: It can't mean the שליח
steps.stepSummary: If the clause is about the שליח, it adds nothing. The ברייתא already allowed him to be on another floor the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the agent: you already said it is valid when he is in the house and the scribe is in the loft, where he can't see him at all. Do you need to say it is valid when he goes in and out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, that the שליח is the one going in and out, and rejects it because the clause would be pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח who is on another floor the whole time is even further away than one who sometimes steps out. Since the ברייתא already allowed the harder case, the easier case does not need to be stated.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if already (introduces 'if X is true, all the more so Y')

phrases.english: If you say it is the agent,
now, when he is in the house and the scribe in the loft,
where he doesn't see him, you said it is valid;
is it necessary to say so when he goes in and out?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to 'who?'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the clause refers to the שליח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The clause would be unneeded, since the ברייתא already allowed a harder case.

steps.title: If it means the סופר, it's obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the clause is about the סופר going in and out, it is obvious. Why would breaks in the writing ruin the גט?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the scribe? That's obvious! Would we disqualify the גט just because he was going in and out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, the סופר, and objects that then the clause teaches something too obvious to need saying. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no reason to think a גט must be written in one sitting. So the ברייתא seems to teach nothing whichever person it means, and the גמרא still has to explain the clause.

keyTerms.meaning: The scribe who writes the גט

steps.confusionAlert: Here the person going in and out would be the סופר, not the שליח. The question is whether stopping in the middle of writing could matter, not whether the שליח saw the writing.

phrases.english: Rather, the scribe? That is obvious!
Because he goes in and out, should we disqualify it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the שליח, tries the סופר and finds that reading obvious too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's clause 'even if he was going in and out all day, it is valid'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the clause is about the סופר, it states something obvious, since breaks in the writing could not disqualify a גט. So the clause seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The scribe went to the market and came back
steps.stepSummary: The clause is needed for a סופר who stepped out to the market. We might have worried that someone there asked him to write a different גט, so the ברייתא tells us not to worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where the סופר went out to the market and came back. You might have said that another person met him there and asked him to write a גט, so he is now writing for a different woman. The ברייתא teaches us not to worry about that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6, which asked why it would be a חידוש that the סופר can go in and out. It explains which case the ברייתא had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Short breaks inside the house really are obvious. But if the סופר went out to the market, someone might have hired him there for a different גט, and then the writing would no longer be לשמה for this woman. The ברייתא tells us we do not suspect this, so the גט is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for… (introduces the special case where a teaching is not obvious)
It teaches us (that the worry is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The סופר may go out to the market and come back to finish the גט. We do not suspect that someone hired him there to write a different גט.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he went out to the market and came back;
you might have said
another person found him
and told him,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves it out, but it means he told the סופר to write a גט for him instead.

phrases.english: it teaches us (that we don't worry about this).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by pointing to a case where the חידוש is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the סופר left the house for the market, not just the room.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: While he was out, someone may have hired him to write a different גט, so the rest of the writing would not be לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not suspect this. The גט is valid.

steps.title: Is בבל like ארץ ישראל or like חוץ לארץ for גיטין?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: רב says בבל counts like ארץ ישראל for גיטין. שמואל says it counts like חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about בבל: רב says it is like ארץ ישראל for גיטין, and שמואל says it is like חוץ לארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about the status of בבל for גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a שליח who brings a גט from חוץ לארץ must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. According to רב, someone bringing a גט from בבל would not need to say it, just like in ארץ ישראל. According to שמואל, he would need to say it.

phrases.english: It was stated: Babylonia;
Rav says: it is like Eretz Yisrael for bills of divorce,
and Shmuel says: like outside the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the ברייתא discussion closed in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: בבל is like ארץ ישראל for גיטין. שמואל: בבל is like חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: Suggestion: they argue over the reason for saying בפני נכתב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב holds the reason is לשמה, and the people of בבל know that well. שמואל holds the reason is קיום, and witnesses from בבל are also hard to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this is their argument? One master, רב, holds that the reason is that people there are not experts in writing a גט לשמה, and the people of בבל are learned. The other master, שמואל, holds that the reason is that witnesses are not available to confirm the signatures, and witnesses from בבל are not often found either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to explain the מחלוקת. It ties it to the earlier argument about why the שליח must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבה said the reason is that people in חוץ לארץ do not know the rules of לשמה. רבא said the reason is that there are no witnesses around to confirm the signatures (קיום). If the reason is לשמה, בבל is like ארץ ישראל, because they are learned there. If the reason is קיום, בבל is like חוץ לארץ, because witnesses from there are still rare.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)
Experts in writing the גט for this specific woman
To confirm it (verifying the witnesses' signatures)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה and רבא. רבה is the one who says the reason is לשמה. רבא is the one who says the reason is קיום.

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ,
phrases.english: that one master holds it is because they are not experts in 'for her sake,'
phrases.notes: This is רב, following רבה's reason for saying בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

phrases.english: and these (the people of Babylonia) are learned;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ,
phrases.english: and one master holds it is because witnesses are not available to confirm it,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל, following רבא's reason.

phrases.english: and these too are not commonly found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests what lies behind the מחלוקת in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רב/שמואל מחלוקת the same as the רבה/רבא argument about the reason for בפני נכתב?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not answered here. Step 10 rejects the suggestion.

steps.title: Rejected: רבה also agrees with רבא's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion. רבה also holds רבא's concern about קיום, so even by רבה's reason בבל would be like חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think that? But רבה also holds the view of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 9. It reminds us that רבה does not say the reason is only לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that רבה agrees with רבא's concern about קיום as well. So even if the people of בבל are experts in לשמה, witnesses from בבל are still rare, and בבל would be like חוץ לארץ. This means רב's view cannot be explained by רבה's reason, and the suggestion falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really think so? (a strong rejection)

steps.whyThisMatters: Once this suggestion is rejected, the גמרא still owes us a new explanation of the רב/שמואל מחלוקת.

phrases.english: And can you think so?!
But Rabba holds the view of Rava!
phrases.notes: Earlier on the daf, the גמרא showed that רבה agrees with רבא's worry about confirming the witnesses, along with his own worry about לשמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא?! הָא רַבָּה אִית לֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that רב follows רבה's reason only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה himself also requires קיום like רבא, so the lack of witnesses in בבל would make it like חוץ לארץ even by his view.

steps.title: Both agree the issue is confirming the signatures
steps.stepSummary: Everyone needs קיום. רב says the ישיבות in בבל make witnesses easy to find. שמואל says the people in the ישיבות are too busy learning to help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that we need to be able to confirm the גט. רב holds that since there are ישיבות, witnesses are easy to find. שמואל holds that the people in the ישיבות are busy with their learning.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 10 pushed away the first explanation of the מחלוקת. Now the גמרא gives a new one: both agree the reason is קיום, and they only argue about the facts in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is no longer about the reason for the rule. Both say the issue is whether witnesses can be found to confirm the signatures. רב thinks the ישיבות bring many people together, so witnesses are easy to find. שמואל thinks those learners are too busy to know people's signatures.

keyTerms.meaning: To confirm it, meaning to check the signatures on the גט
ישיבות, the places where people gather to learn

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees we need to be able to confirm it;
Rav holds: since there are ישיבות,
witnesses are easily found;
and Shmuel holds:
the people of the ישיבות are busy with their learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was pushed away in step 10 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument from the reason for the rule to the facts in בבל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל argue over whether the reason is לשמה or קיום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both hold the reason is קיום. They argue over whether the ישיבות make witnesses easy to find.

steps.title: Support for רב from רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that ever since רב came to בבל, they treated בבל like ארץ ישראל for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא: We made ourselves in בבל like ארץ ישראל for גיטין, from the time רב came to בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement that backs up רב's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reports that the practice in בבל changed once רב arrived. This fits רב's view, since his coming built up the learning there, and that is what makes witnesses easy to find.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, used to bring support
We made ourselves, meaning we treated ourselves as

phrases.english: It was also stated,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: עָשִׂינוּ עַצְמֵינוּ בְּבָבֶל כְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגִיטִּין,
phrases.english: We made ourselves in Babylonia like Eretz Yisrael for bills of divorce,
from when Rav came to Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's side of the explanation just given.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that בבל is like ארץ ישראל for גיטין
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's report, in the name of רבי אבא, about the practice in בבל after רב arrived

steps.title: בבל is north of the border
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes רבי יהודה: everything past עכו to the north is outside the border. בבל is to the north, so it should be outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה challenged: רבי יהודה says, from רקם eastward is outside, and רקם counts as east. From אשקלון southward is outside, and אשקלון counts as south. From עכו northward is outside, and עכו counts as north. But בבל is north of ארץ ישראל, as the פסוק says: 'Out of the north the evil shall break forth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רב's view. A משנה sets the borders of ארץ ישראל for גיטין, and בבל falls outside them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה sets the border on each side. Even עכו itself counts as outside on the north side. The פסוק in ירמיה shows that בבל counts as 'north', so it must be outside too. Then how can רב treat בבל like ארץ ישראל?

keyTerms.meaning: The place marking the eastern border
Akko, the city marking the northern border
But look, used to start an argument

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya challenged:
Rabbi Yehuda says: from Rekem eastward is outside,
and Rekem itself is like the east;
from Ashkelon southward is outside, and Ashkelon is like the south;
from Akko northward is outside, and Akko is like the north.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בָּבֶל לִצְפוֹנָהּ דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָיְימָא,
phrases.english: But Babylonia lies to the north of Eretz Yisrael,
as it is written: 'Then ה׳ said to me,
out of the north the evil shall break forth,'
phrases.notes: ירמיה 1:14. The evil there comes from בבל, so the פסוק calls בבל 'north'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of רב that was just supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that בבל is like ארץ ישראל for גיטין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everything north of עכו is outside the border. בבל is north, so it should be like חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר only included nearby עכו
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says עכו counts like ארץ ישראל, but only because it is close. Far-away בבל would not count, even for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned: רבי מאיר says עכו is like ארץ ישראל for גיטין. Even רבי מאיר only said this about עכו, which is close. But בבל, which is far away, does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה makes his challenge stronger. Even the more lenient opinion of רבי מאיר could not include בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might try to rely on רבי מאיר, who disagrees with רבי יהודה about עכו. But רבי מאיר only included עכו because it sits right by the border. בבל is far away, so no one in the משנה treats it like ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: And we learned: Rabbi Meir says:
Akko is like Eretz Yisrael for bills of divorce;
and even Rabbi Meir said this
only about Akko, which is close,
but Babylonia, which is far, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same challenge and blocks an escape through רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the lenient view only includes places near the border. בבל is far, so no one includes it.

steps.title: בבל is an exception
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers his own challenge: the border rule applies to every place except בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the challenge and he answered it: except for בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The same רבי ירמיה who asked the question now answers it. בבל is left out of the border rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's borders are true in general, but בבל is an exception. So רב's ruling still stands, even though בבל sits to the north.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He asked the question and he answered it himself

steps.whatToRemember: רב treats בבל like ארץ ישראל for גיטין because the ישיבות make witnesses for קיום easy to find. שמואל disagrees. The border rule in the משנה does not include בבל, which is an exception.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say that בבל is part of ארץ ישראל on the map. It only says that בבל is an exception to the border rule for גיטין.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the challenge and he resolved it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי ירמיה, the one who asked the question.

phrases.english: except for Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 13 and 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Makes an exception to the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everything north of עכו, including בבל, is outside for גיטין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The border rule applies everywhere except בבל, so רב's ruling stands.

steps.title: Where does בבל end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far the borders of בבל reach for the rule that it counts like ארץ ישראל for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until where does בבל go?
steps.whatsHappening: We just learned that בבל is treated like ארץ ישראל for גיטין, so the גמרא now asks where בבל's borders are. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בבל gets a special rule, we need to know exactly which towns count as בבל. A גט brought from a town inside בבל would not need the declaration בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, but a גט from a town outside it would.

keyTerms.meaning: Until where; how far does it reach
Babylonia, where the great ישיבות of the אמוראים were

phrases.english: Until where is Babylonia?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that בבל is treated like ארץ ישראל and asks for its exact borders.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The geographic limits of בבל for the purpose of גיטין.

steps.title: רב פפא: the same argument as for family lineage
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the borders of בבל for גיטין are argued about in the same way as its borders for יוחסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: just as there is an argument about the borders for family lineage, there is the same argument for גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The same argument about בבל's borders for family lineage applies to גיטין too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a known argument about where בבל ends for יוחסין, the question of which families have a trusted lineage. רב פפא does not create a new map for גיטין. He reuses the same borders, so the same argument carries over.

keyTerms.meaning: Family lineage; whether a family has a trusted, clean ancestry

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Like the argument regarding lineage,
phrases.notes: This is a known argument about how far בבל goes for family lineage. It is discussed in מסכת קידושין.

phrases.english: so is the argument regarding bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question of בבל's borders.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The borders of בבל for גיטין follow the same argument as the borders for יוחסין.

steps.title: רב יוסף: for גיטין everyone agrees on the bridge
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the argument is only about יוחסין. For גיטין everyone agrees that בבל extends up to the second arch of the bridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the argument is only about lineage. For bills of divorce, everyone agrees that בבל goes up to the second arch of the bridge.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different answer from רב פפא. He keeps the lineage argument separate and gives one agreed border for גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב פפא, the borders for גיטין are disputed just like the borders for יוחסין. For רב יוסף, the two topics are separate. For גיטין there is no dispute: the border is a fixed point, the second arch of the bridge.

keyTerms.meaning: The second arch (literally, the second boat)

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
The argument is regarding lineage,
but regarding bills of divorce, everyone agrees:
until the second arch of the bridge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר מַחֲלוֹקֶת לְיוּחֲסִין אֲבָל לְגִיטִּין דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפא by separating גיטין from the lineage argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For גיטין, everyone agrees that בבל reaches the second arch of the bridge.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a border can be defined differently for different areas of הלכה, depending on the reason behind each rule.

steps.title: רב חסדא's one-way requirement
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא required the declaration for a גט brought from אקטיספון to בי ארדשיר, but not for one brought from בי ארדשיר to אקטיספון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא required the agent to make the declaration when bringing a גט from אקטיספון to בי ארדשיר. When bringing one from בי ארדשיר to אקטיספון, he did not require it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a ruling of רב חסדא about two nearby towns. The agent had to make the declaration in one direction but not in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a rule like this depends on the place where the גט was written. Here the same pair of towns gets a different result depending on which way the גט travels. That puzzle sets up the next steps, which look for the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires (here, requires the agent to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם)
A town, one side of the case
A neighboring town, the other side of the case

phrases.english: Rav Chisda required
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves it out, but he means he required the agent to say 'it was written and signed in front of me.'

phrases.english: from Akteisfon to Bei Ardeshir,
but from Bei Ardeshir to Akteisfon
he did not require it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא מַצְרֵיךְ מֵאַקְטֵיסְפוֹן לְבֵי אַרְדָּשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the borders of בבל to a specific ruling about two neighboring towns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration is required for a גט going from אקטיספון to בי ארדשיר, but not for one going from בי ארדשיר to אקטיספון.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the direction straight. The declaration is needed only when the גט comes FROM אקטיספון. A גט coming from בי ארדשיר needs no declaration.

steps.title: Is it because בי ארדשיר knows about לשמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב חסדא holds the reason for the declaration is that people are not experts in לשמה, and the people of בי ארדשיר are learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that he holds the reason is that people are not experts in writing a גט for her sake, and these people of בי ארדשיר are learned in it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation for רב חסדא's ruling. It ties his ruling to the reason that people don't know the laws of לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, two reasons were given for the declaration: people don't know the laws of לשמה (רבה), or we need the signatures confirmed (רבא). If לשמה is the reason, a גט from learned בי ארדשיר would need no declaration. If the people of אקטיספון are not learned, a גט from there would need one.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
For her sake; the גט must be written specifically for this woman

phrases.english: Shall we say he holds
that it is because they are not experts in writing it for her sake,
and these people are learned?
phrases.notes: 'These' means the people of בי ארדשיר. That is why a גט from their town needs no declaration.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא קָסָבַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain רב חסדא's ruling using the לשמה reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב חסדא's ruling shows that he holds the declaration exists because of the לשמה reason.

steps.title: But רבה also agrees with רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: even רבה, who gave the לשמה reason, agrees with רבא that קיום is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think that? But רבה also holds like רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the suggestion it just made. It reminds us that even רבה agrees we need קיום, so being learned in לשמה is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we established that even רבה, who stressed לשמה, also accepts רבא's reason of קיום. So even if the people of בי ארדשיר are experts in לשמה, the signatures would still need confirming. Their learning alone cannot explain why their גט is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a sharp rejection)

phrases.english: And can you really think that?!
But רבה holds like רבא!
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier conclusion that everyone, even רבה, needs the signatures confirmed (קיום).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא וְהָא רַבָּה אִית לֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the לשמה explanation offered in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב חסדא's ruling rests only on the לשמה reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since even רבה requires קיום, being learned in לשמה cannot exempt a גט from the declaration.

steps.title: The real reason: who knows whose signatures
steps.stepSummary: Everyone requires קיום. The people of אקטיספון know the signatures of בי ארדשיר, because those people come to their market, but not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees we need to confirm the signatures. The people of בי ארדשיר go to the market in אקטיספון, so the people of אקטיספון recognize their signatures. But the people of בי ארדשיר do not recognize the signatures of the people of אקטיספון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real explanation for רב חסדא's ruling. It is about who recognizes whose signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because קיום is the issue, what matters is whether people in the receiving town can identify the witnesses' signatures. In אקטיספון they know the signatures of בי ארדשיר, so a גט arriving there can be confirmed without the declaration. In בי ארדשיר they don't know the signatures of אקטיספון, so the agent must make the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: Confirming the signatures on a document

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees we need to confirm it;
and these people, since they go to the market over there,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the people of בי ארדשיר, and 'over there' is אקטיספון.

phrases.english: those people know the signatures of these people,
phrases.notes: The people of אקטיספון recognize the signatures of the people of בי ארדשיר.

phrases.english: but these do not know those people's signatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected לשמה explanation with an explanation based on קיום.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the reason behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's ruling was based on the people of בי ארדשיר being learned in לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is based on קיום: the receiving town either knows the signatures from the sending town, or it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the need for the declaration depends on whether the signatures can be confirmed, which can differ from town to town.

steps.title: Why בי ארדשיר doesn't know the signatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people of בי ארדשיר don't recognize the signatures of אקטיספון, and answers that they are busy with their own market.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? They are busy with their own market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks one quick question and answers it right away, explaining why the knowledge goes only one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that since the people of בי ארדשיר trade with אקטיספון, both towns would know each other's signatures. The answer is that when they go to market, they are busy buying and selling. They don't take the time to learn the signatures of the people there. Meanwhile, the locals of אקטיספון have time to get to know them.
steps.whatToRemember: For גיטין, everyone requires קיום. So רב חסדא's one-way rule depends on which town's people recognize the other town's signatures, not on who knows the laws of לשמה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
They are busy with their market.
phrases.notes: The people of בי ארדשיר are busy with their business, so they don't learn the signatures of the people of אקטיספון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the one-sided knowledge described in the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The people of בי ארדשיר are too busy with their market dealings to learn the signatures of the people of אקטיספון.

steps.title: Three אמוראים make the declaration rule stricter, even inside one town
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה required the declaration from one side of the street to the other. רב ששת required it from one group of houses to another. רבא required it even within the same group of houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה required the declaration even from one side of the road to the other. רב ששת required it even from one group of houses to another. And רבא required it even within the same group of houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports three אמוראים who each required the agent to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם even over very short distances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about bringing a גט between different places. Here the rule is pushed further, step by step: across the street, then between neighborhoods, and finally within one neighborhood. רבא is the strictest of the three.

keyTerms.meaning: one side of the public road
a group of houses, a neighborhood
within the same group of houses

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh would require [the declaration]
from one side to the other side;
phrases.notes: Picture a public road running through town: this means just crossing from one side of it to the other.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would require it
from one group of houses to another group;
and Rava required it within the same group of houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ מַצְרֵיךְ מֵעַרְסָא לְעַרְסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of practical rulings about when the declaration is needed, following רב חסדא's ruling, and narrows the distance down to within one town.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration can be required even within a single town: across the road (רבה בר אבוה), between neighborhoods (רב ששת), and even within one neighborhood (רבא).

steps.title: רבא's own reason does not seem to fit his strict ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא can require the declaration within one neighborhood, when he holds the reason is that witnesses are not available to confirm the signatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא is the one who said the reason for the declaration is that witnesses are not available to confirm the גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling from Step 24 by pointing to his own reason for the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that the declaration replaces קיום, since witnesses who can confirm the signatures are hard to find. Within the same neighborhood, though, the witnesses should be right there, so the reason seems to fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: to confirm it (to verify the signatures)

phrases.english: But Rava is the one who said
[the reason is] because witnesses are not available to confirm it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in Step 24 using his own stated reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's requirement of the declaration within the same neighborhood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the declaration exists only because confirming witnesses are hard to find, then inside one neighborhood, where witnesses are close by, it should not be needed.

steps.title: The people of מחוזא move around
steps.stepSummary: The people of מחוזא are different because they are always on the move, so even the neighborhood witnesses may not be available.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of מחוזא are different, because they move around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: רבא's ruling was made for his town, מחוזא, where people constantly move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason stays the same: witnesses are not available. In מחוזא, people move so often that even the witnesses from the same neighborhood may already be gone. So his reason fully applies there.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's strict ruling does not change his reason. It applies that reason to a town whose people keep moving, where witnesses really cannot be found.

phrases.english: The people of Mechoza are different,
since they move around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a local situation (מחוזא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Within one neighborhood witnesses are always available, so רבא's reason should not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: In מחוזא people move constantly, so witnesses are not available even nearby, and רבא's reason applies.

steps.title: רב חנין's story: רב כהנא brings a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב חנין relates that רב כהנא brought a גט. He does not remember whether it went from סורא to נהרדעא or from נהרדעא to סורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנין relates: רב כהנא brought a גט, and I do not know whether it was from סורא to נהרדעא or from נהרדעא to סורא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. This line sets up the scene for the question רב כהנא will ask רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that רב חנין is unsure of the direction is important. As in רב חסדא's ruling (Step 19), the direction of travel could matter. The story will show how רב ruled in a case between these two cities.

phrases.english: Rav Chanin relates:
Rav Kahana brought a bill of divorce,
and I do not know
whether [it was] from Sura to Neharde'a,
or from Neharde'a to Sura.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new practical case after the discussion of distances within a town.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a גט brought between סורא and נהרדעא, with the direction uncertain.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks רב whether he must say the declaration
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא came before רב and asked whether he needed to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב and said to him: Do I need to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' or don't I?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, רב כהנא asks רב a practical question: does this גט need the declaration?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between two different cities, one might assume the declaration is needed. רב כהנא is unsure, so he asks a leading authority before handing over the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was written in my presence and signed in my presence": the agent's declaration

phrases.english: He came before Rav,
he said to him:
Am I required to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,"
or am I not required?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צְרִיכְנָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by stating רב כהנא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an agent bringing a גט between סורא and נהרדעא must say the declaration.

steps.title: רב answers: you do not need to
steps.stepSummary: רב told רב כהנא that he did not need to say the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are not required.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers רב כהנא's question: no declaration is needed for this גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the גט traveled between two separate cities, רב ruled that the declaration was not required. רב's answer continues on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume every trip between two cities needs the declaration. Here רב says it is not needed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
You are not required,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב rules that the declaration is not required for this גט between סורא and נהרדעא.
